intent.raw_query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026

experiences.name: Phi Phi Islands Snorkeling & Island Hopping Tour
experiences.description: Join a full-day speedboat tour departing from Krabi or Ao Nang to explore the stunning Phi Phi Islands. Snorkel at Maya Bay, visit Monkey Beach, and swim in crystal-clear turquoise waters. Book accommodation in Ao Nang or Krabi Town to minimize travel time to the pier. Ideal from Day 2 onward to allow recovery from late arrival.

experiences.name: Railay Beach Rock Climbing & Sunset Exploration
experiences.description: Take a short longtail boat ride from Ao Nang to the car-free Railay Beach peninsula. Spend the afternoon rock climbing on limestone karsts with a certified guide, then relax on Railay West Beach for a breathtaking sunset. Staying in Ao Nang keeps this experience within 15 minutes by boat, making it highly accessible.

experiences.name: Chiang Mai Night Bazaar Street Food Walk
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Night Bazaar and Warorot Market in Chiang Mai's city center, sampling iconic northern Thai street food including Khao Soi curry noodles, Sai Oua sausage, and mango sticky rice. Stay in the Old City or Nimman area for easy walking access. Schedule this experience on Day 2 of your Chiang Mai leg to settle in on arrival day.

experiences.name: Koh Lanta Full-Day Beach Hopping by Scooter
experiences.description: Rent a scooter and self-explore Koh Lanta's quieter, less-crowded beaches including Klong Dao, Long Beach, and Bamboo Bay. Stop at beachside shacks for fresh grilled seafood and coconuts. Choose guesthouses along Klong Dao Beach to be centrally located for easy access to all beaches without long transfers.

experiences.name: Bangkok Floating Market & Street Food Tuk-Tuk Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided tuk-tuk tour through Bangkok's Thonburi district, visiting Taling Chan Floating Market to taste fresh pad thai, grilled river prawns, and tropical fruits directly from boat vendors. This experience is best placed on Day 2 in Bangkok, allowing Day 1 evening (late flight arrival) for rest. Stay in the Silom or Riverside area for quick access to the Chao Phraya express boat to Thonburi.
experiences.location: Taling Chan Floating Market, Thonburi, Bangkok

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Thailand
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Krabi Airport at 13:00. Take a shared minivan or songthaew (local red truck taxi) to your Krabi Province Boutique Stay - budget around 150-200 THB per person. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along Maharat Road to get oriented with the town center.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Krabi Town Night Market (Thanon Khong Ka) along the riverside. Browse street food stalls, pick up snacks, and soak in the local atmosphere. Walk along the Krabi River promenade and enjoy the mangrove views at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a roadside stall near your accommodation - try Khao Man Gai (chicken rice) for around 50-60 THB
meals.dinner: Krabi Town Night Market - load up on pad thai, mango sticky rice, grilled satay, and fresh spring rolls for under 150 THB total

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency at the airport for a decent rate or use a local ATM. Buy a local SIM card (AIS or DTAC) at the airport for around 299 THB for 30 days of data. October is the tail end of the rainy season in Krabi - pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and head to the Krabi Town Morning Market (Talat Kao) for a classic Thai breakfast experience. Browse fresh tropical fruits, noodle soups, and local pastries. Afterward, visit Wat Kaew Korawaram, the prominent white temple on the hill overlooking Krabi Town - free entry and great views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hire a longtail boat from the Chao Fa Pier for a half-day mangrove tour through the Krabi River estuary. Visit the famous mangrove forest and the Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Sua) - climb the 1,237 steps to the summit for panoramic views of Krabi Province. Shared boat tours cost around 300-400 THB per person.
day_by_day.evening: Return to town and relax at a riverside café. Head to the Chao Fa Pier night market for dinner and watch longtail boats drift past as the sun sets over the mangroves.

meals.breakfast: Krabi Morning Market - bowl of Jok (rice porridge) or Kuay Tiew (noodle soup) for 40-60 THB
meals.lunch: Pack snacks from the morning market or grab a quick meal from a street stall near Tiger Cave Temple for 60-80 THB
meals.dinner: Chao Fa Pier area street food - grilled fish, som tum (papaya salad), and sticky rice for around 120-150 THB

day_by_day.notes: Start the Tiger Cave Temple climb early in the afternoon to avoid peak heat. Bring plenty of water and wear comfortable shoes. The climb takes about 45-60 minutes each way.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early shared songthaew from Krabi Town to Railay Beach (via Ao Nang, then longtail boat). The longtail boat from Ao Nang to Railay costs around 100 THB per person. Arrive early to enjoy Railay West Beach before the crowds. Explore the dramatic limestone cliffs and turquoise water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek through the jungle to Railay Viewpoint for stunning panoramic views of the peninsula. Afterward, visit Phra Nang Cave Beach - one of Thailand's most beautiful beaches with a sacred princess shrine inside the cave. Swim and snorkel in the crystal-clear water.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Ao Nang via longtail boat and explore the Ao Nang Walking Street for dinner and evening entertainment. Browse souvenir shops and enjoy the lively beach town atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Eat at your guesthouse or grab a quick breakfast from a street stall in Krabi Town before departing - roti with banana and condensed milk for 40 THB
meals.lunch: Pack fruit and snacks, or grab a simple meal at one of the beachside restaurants on Railay - budget around 150-200 THB
meals.dinner: Ao Nang Walking Street - try fresh seafood BBQ, green curry, and a fresh coconut for around 200 THB

day_by_day.notes: Longtail boats from Ao Nang to Railay run frequently throughout the day. Last boats back to Ao Nang typically leave around 18:00-19:00. Railay is only accessible by boat as it is surrounded by cliffs.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget group tour for a 4 Islands snorkeling trip departing from Ao Nang or Krabi Town pier. Islands typically visited include Koh Mor, Koh Chuak, Koh Mah, and Koh Talabeng. Group tours cost around 500-700 THB per person including snorkel gear and longtail boat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the island-hopping tour - snorkel at coral reefs, swim in emerald lagoons, and explore pristine beaches. Have lunch on one of the islands (usually included or available for purchase at a small beach shack).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi Town by late afternoon. Visit the Vogue Night Bazaar or the weekend walking street if available. Rest and recharge for the next day.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure - simple toast, eggs, and coffee at a guesthouse café for 80-100 THB
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch on the island - fresh grilled fish or fried rice at a beachside shack for 150-200 THB
meals.dinner: Back in Krabi Town - visit a local Thai restaurant and try Massaman curry with rice for 80-100 THB

day_by_day.notes: Book the 4 Islands tour the day before through your guesthouse or a local tour operator to get the best price. Bring sunscreen, a waterproof bag, and a change of dry clothes. October weather may bring occasional rain showers - check conditions in the morning.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day to Koh Lanta. Take a shared minivan or ferry from Krabi Town to Koh Lanta (around 350-450 THB, approximately 2-2.5 hours). Check into a budget bungalow on Long Beach (Haad Phra Ae) - rooms available from 400-600 THB per night.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a scooter (150-200 THB per day) and explore Koh Lanta's coastline. Visit Long Beach for a swim, then ride south to discover quieter beaches like Klong Nin Beach and Kantiang Bay. Stop at viewpoints along the way for scenic photos.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Old Town (Ban Ko Lanta) on the east coast - a charming stilted fishing village with colorful shophouses, sea gypsies heritage, and excellent seafood restaurants along the waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Eat in Krabi before departing - street stall noodles or rice with egg for 50-60 THB
meals.lunch: Grab a bite at a beachside shack on Long Beach upon arrival - pad thai or fried rice for 80-100 THB
meals.dinner: Old Town waterfront restaurants - fresh grilled seafood platter and a cold Chang beer for around 250-300 THB

day_by_day.notes: Confirm ferry and minivan schedules the day before as they can change seasonally. Koh Lanta is more relaxed and less crowded than Phi Phi, making it ideal for budget travelers. Scooter rental is the most cost-effective way to explore the island.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and drive your scooter to the southern tip of Koh Lanta to visit Mu Ko Lanta National Park (entry fee 200 THB for foreigners). Explore the lighthouse, jungle trails, and beautiful viewpoints overlooking the Andaman Sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkel at the national park's coral reefs or relax at the secluded beach near the park entrance. Ride back north and stop at Klong Dao Beach for a swim. Visit a local market in Ban Sala Dan (the main village) for fresh tropical fruits and snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from Long Beach - one of the best sunset spots on Koh Lanta. Join other travelers at a beachfront bar for a happy hour drink (cocktails from 100-150 THB during happy hour). Enjoy a relaxed evening at a beach restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit smoothie and toast at a beach café on Long Beach for 80-100 THB
meals.lunch: Pack snacks from the market or eat at a simple restaurant near the national park for 100-120 THB
meals.dinner: Beachfront restaurant on Long Beach - BBQ seafood, green papaya salad, and coconut rice for 200-250 THB

day_by_day.notes: The national park is best visited in the morning before it gets too hot. Bring insect repellent for the jungle trails. The lighthouse area offers some of the most dramatic scenery on the island.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget snorkeling day trip to the islands around Koh Lanta - typically visiting Koh Rok Noi, Koh Rok Yai, and Koh Haa. These islands have some of the clearest water and best coral reefs in the region. Group tours cost around 700-900 THB including equipment and lunch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue snorkeling and island exploration. Koh Haa (Five Islands) is a highlight with an underwater cave system and incredible marine biodiversity. Swim with tropical fish, sea turtles, and vibrant coral gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Koh Lanta by late afternoon. Treat yourself to a traditional Thai massage on the beach (300-400 THB for 1 hour). Enjoy a quiet evening dinner and prepare for the next leg of the journey.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the guesthouse or a nearby café - eggs, toast, and coffee for 100 THB
meals.lunch: Included with the snorkeling tour - typically a simple Thai lunch on the boat or a beach island
meals.dinner: Local Thai restaurant away from the beach strip - order a set meal of rice, curry, and vegetable stir-fry for 120-150 THB

day_by_day.notes: Book the snorkeling trip the evening before. Koh Rok is part of a national park so an additional entry fee of 200 THB may apply. These southern islands have some of Thailand's best snorkeling but can be affected by weather in October.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day to Koh Phi Phi. Take the ferry from Koh Lanta to Koh Phi Phi Don (around 350-450 THB, approximately 1.5-2 hours). Check into a budget guesthouse or dorm on Phi Phi - dorms from 300-400 THB, private rooms from 600-800 THB. Drop your bags and head straight to Loh Dalum Bay viewpoint for the iconic panoramic shot of Phi Phi.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Phi Phi Don on foot - the island has no cars or motorbikes. Visit Tonsai Village, browse the market stalls, and walk to the quieter Loh Bakao Beach on the north side of the island for a swim away from the crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the legendary Phi Phi nightlife at Loh Dalum Bay - fire shows on the beach, beach bars, and a vibrant backpacker scene. Enjoy a bucket cocktail (200-250 THB) and watch the fire jugglers perform.

meals.breakfast: Eat in Koh Lanta before the ferry - roti with egg and tea for 60-80 THB
meals.lunch: Quick lunch at a Tonsai Village restaurant upon arrival - pad see ew or fried rice for 100-120 THB
meals.dinner: Beachfront restaurant at Loh Dalum Bay - grilled fish with garlic and lime, rice, and a cold beer for 200-250 THB

day_by_day.notes: Koh Phi Phi is more expensive than Koh Lanta due to its popularity. Book accommodation in advance. Store valuables securely as petty theft can occur in busy tourist areas. The viewpoint hike takes about 20-30 minutes and is best done in the late afternoon for golden hour light.

day_by_day.morning: Hire a longtail boat for a half-day tour to Maya Bay on Koh Phi Phi Leh (the island made famous by the movie The Beach). Entry fee applies (400 THB for foreigners). The bay reopened with strict visitor limits to protect coral restoration - arrive early for the best experience. Snorkel at Pileh Lagoon and Loh Samah Bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Phi Phi Don and rent a kayak (150-200 THB per hour) to explore the sea caves and hidden lagoons around the island at your own pace. Paddle to Viking Cave (Tham Phaya Nak) to see ancient cave paintings and swiftlet nests.
day_by_day.evening: Climb to the Phi Phi Viewpoint for a spectacular sunset over both bays of the island. Join the crowd of travelers for one of Thailand's most iconic views. Head back down for a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Fruit smoothie bowl and coffee at a Tonsai café for 120-150 THB
meals.lunch: Pack snacks for the boat trip or eat at a beachside stall on Phi Phi Leh if available - 100-150 THB
meals.dinner: Night market stalls in Tonsai Village - spring rolls, satay skewers, mango sticky rice for under 200 THB total

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has strict visitor limits and timed entry slots - book through a licensed tour operator. Swimming inside Maya Bay may be restricted to protect coral restoration. The viewpoint is free but the path can be slippery after rain - wear proper footwear.

day_by_day.morning: Travel back to Krabi Province via ferry (around 350-400 THB, 1.5 hours). Check back into your Krabi Province Boutique Stay. Freshen up and visit the Krabi Town Weekend Market (if it falls on the right day) or explore the local shops and cafés along Maharaj Road.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Shell Cemetery (Susan Hoi) - a unique geological formation of 75-million-year-old fossilized shells forming a natural reef ledge. Entry is free and it is only about 17 km from Krabi Town. Afterward, stop at Ao Nam Mao Beach nearby for a quiet swim.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening back in Krabi Town. Visit the riverside walking street and treat yourself to a traditional Thai herbal steam bath or foot massage at a local spa (200-300 THB for 45 minutes).

meals.breakfast: Eat before the ferry departs - grab a banana roti from a street cart for 40-50 THB
meals.lunch: Local Thai restaurant near the Shell Cemetery or back in Krabi Town - khao pad (fried rice) with chicken for 80-100 THB
meals.dinner: Riverside restaurant in Krabi Town - try a full Thai meal with tom yum soup, stir-fried vegetables, and jasmine rice for 150-200 THB

day_by_day.notes: The ferry back to Krabi from Phi Phi runs multiple times daily - morning departures are recommended. Confirm your return ferry ticket the evening before. The Shell Cemetery is best visited by renting a scooter or taking a songthaew from Krabi Town.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Koh Hong Island (not to be confused with the one in Phang Nga Bay). Join a budget longtail boat group tour from Ao Nam Mao Pier - costs around 400-500 THB per person. Explore the stunning hidden lagoon enclosed by towering limestone karsts, accessible only at certain tide levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the island-hopping around the Hong Islands group - snorkel at coral reefs, swim in emerald water, and relax on white sand beaches. The area is less crowded than Phi Phi and the water clarity is excellent.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi Town in the late afternoon. Visit the Chao Fa Pier area for sunset views over the river and mangroves. Have a leisurely dinner and explore the local night bazaar.

meals.breakfast: Morning market breakfast in Krabi Town - Khao Tom (rice soup) with egg and ginger for 50-60 THB
meals.lunch: Pack fruit and snacks from the morning market, or buy simple food from the tour boat for 100-150 THB
meals.dinner: Local restaurant in Krabi Town - order a full Thai set meal with soup, curry, and stir-fry for 150-180 THB

day_by_day.notes: Koh Hong is best visited during high tide when the lagoon is accessible by kayak or swimming. The tour operator will advise on tide times. Bring an underwater camera or waterproof phone case for the lagoon experience.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day cooking class in Krabi Town to learn authentic Thai cuisine. Budget cooking classes start from around 800-1,000 THB and typically include a market tour, hands-on cooking of 4-5 dishes, and a meal. Learn to make pad thai, green curry, tom kha gai, and mango sticky rice.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Krabi's Emerald Pool (Sa Morakot) and the Blue Pool (Sa Nam Phet) in the Thung Teao Forest Natural Park, about 45 km from Krabi Town. Entry fee is 200 THB for foreigners. The natural hot spring pools and jungle trails make for a magical afternoon. Take a songthaew or join a shared tour for around 300-400 THB return.
day_by_day.evening: Final night of major exploration in Krabi. Head to the night market for souvenir shopping and a farewell street food feast. Try everything you might have missed - fried insects (adventurous!), fresh coconut ice cream, and Thai iced tea.

meals.breakfast: Included with the cooking class market tour, or eat beforehand at a street stall for 50-60 THB
meals.lunch: Eat the dishes you cooked in the cooking class - a full Thai meal included in the class fee
meals.dinner: Krabi Night Market grand finale - spend 200-250 THB on a spread of your favorite Thai street foods

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class in advance through your guesthouse. The Emerald Pool is best visited in the morning to avoid crowds but an afternoon visit is also beautiful. The forest park closes at 17:00 so plan accordingly. Wear swimwear under your clothes for a dip in the natural pools.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Krabi. Wake up early for one last sunrise walk along the Krabi River promenade. Visit the morning market one final time for breakfast and pick up any last-minute snacks or souvenirs. Pack your bags and check out of the Krabi Province Boutique Stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, take a shared songthaew or minivan to Krabi Airport (150-200 THB). Allow at least 2 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Browse the airport shops for last-minute Thai snacks, dried fruits, and coconut products to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Krabi Airport. Reflect on 13 incredible days of beaches, island hopping, and street food adventures across one of Thailand's most beautiful provinces.

meals.breakfast: Final Thai breakfast at the morning market - Khao Niao Mamuang (mango sticky rice) and fresh coconut for 60-80 THB
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport or grab snacks from the market to eat on the go - 100-150 THB
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Check your flight departure time carefully and arrange airport transport the evening before. Budget travelers tip: buy Thai snacks like dried mango, coconut chips, and instant Thai noodles at the local market before heading to the airport - they make great gifts and are much cheaper than airport shops. Keep some Thai Baht for airport taxes or last-minute expenses.

trip_options.title: Classic Thailand Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — skip morning activities. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and arrange airport transfer to your Krabi Province Boutique Stay. Enjoy the scenic drive through lush limestone karst landscapes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your boutique hotel, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation stroll around Krabi Town. Visit the iconic Krabi Town Walking Street area and the riverside promenade along the Krabi River to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Chao Fah Pier night market for a vibrant introduction to Krabi's street food scene. Browse stalls selling grilled seafood, pad thai, mango sticky rice, and fresh coconut drinks while soaking in the local atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a roadside restaurant during transfer — try khao man gai (chicken rice) for around 60–80 THB
meals.dinner: Chao Fah Pier Night Market — grilled prawns, pad see ew, and fresh fruit shakes. Budget 200–350 THB per person

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Exchange some currency at the airport for a better rate than in town. October is the tail end of green season in Krabi; expect occasional rain showers but fewer crowds and lush scenery.

day_by_day.morning: Early visit to Wat Tham Seua (Tiger Cave Temple). Climb the famous 1,237 steps to the summit for panoramic views over Krabi's karst landscape and rice paddies — an unforgettable sunrise or early morning experience. Entrance is free; wear comfortable shoes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to town and hire a longtail boat from Chao Fah Pier for a half-day tour of the Krabi mangroves and sea caves, including the famous Bor Thor mangrove kayaking area. Glide through tunnel-like mangrove passages and spot wildlife. Tours run approximately 500–800 THB per person.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Krabi Town's vibrant Th Maharat Road for street food dinner. Try local southern Thai dishes at one of the open-air restaurants near the night market.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel or a nearby café — try khao tom (rice porridge) with sides for 80–120 THB
meals.lunch: Pack snacks or eat at a local restaurant near Tiger Cave — som tum (papaya salad) and grilled chicken for 120–180 THB
meals.dinner: Th Maharat Road street stalls — massaman curry, roti with condensed milk, and fresh coconut ice cream. Budget 200–300 THB per person

day_by_day.notes: Start the Tiger Cave climb by 7:00 AM to beat the heat and catch the best light. Bring plenty of water and a small towel. The mangrove kayak tour is best booked through your hotel for a vetted operator.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day 4-Island Tour departing from Krabi Town pier. First stop: Tup Island (Koh Tup) — a stunning sandbar connecting two islands at low tide. Snorkel the clear waters and explore the sandbar on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the island-hopping tour to Chicken Island (Koh Kai) for more snorkeling and swimming, then Poda Island (Koh Poda) for a beach picnic lunch included in the tour. Relax on white sand beaches surrounded by turquoise water and dramatic limestone cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi Town by late afternoon. Rest at the hotel, then head out for dinner at a local restaurant. Try Ruen Mai Restaurant, one of Krabi's most beloved mid-range spots for authentic southern Thai cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick stop at a local bakery — coffee and toast with eggs for 100–150 THB
meals.lunch: Included in the 4-Island Tour package (simple beach picnic with rice, grilled fish, and fruit)
meals.dinner: Ruen Mai Restaurant — gaeng som (sour curry), stir-fried morning glory, and steamed rice. Budget 300–450 THB per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the 4-Island Tour the day before through your hotel or a local agency. Cost is typically 700–1,200 THB per person including longtail boat, snorkeling gear, and lunch. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a dry bag, and a rash guard.

day_by_day.morning: Take a ferry from Krabi Town pier to Koh Lanta (approximately 1.5–2 hours). Check in to a day-use arrangement or simply drop bags at a beach café. Head straight to Long Beach (Hat Khlong Dao) for a relaxed morning swim and beachcombing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a scooter (150–200 THB/day) and explore Koh Lanta's west coast. Visit the Old Town (Ban Ko Lanta) — a charming stilted fishing village with wooden shophouses, local craft shops, and sea-facing cafés. Browse the small galleries and try fresh seafood at the waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the famous Koh Lanta sunset from Sunset Bar or one of the beachfront restaurants along Long Beach. Enjoy cocktails and grilled seafood as the sky turns golden over the Andaman Sea. Return to Krabi by evening ferry or stay overnight if budget allows.

meals.breakfast: Eat before the ferry or grab something at Krabi pier — congee or a banana roti for 60–100 THB
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at Old Town Koh Lanta — grilled barracuda, rice, and a cold Chang beer. Budget 250–400 THB per person
meals.dinner: Beachfront restaurant on Long Beach — mixed seafood platter, green curry, and coconut shake. Budget 350–500 THB per person

day_by_day.notes: Ferry schedules vary by season — confirm departure times the night before. If staying overnight on Koh Lanta, budget guesthouses on Long Beach run 800–1,500 THB/night. October can bring afternoon rain; mornings are typically clearer.

day_by_day.morning: If still on Koh Lanta: visit Mu Ko Lanta National Park at the southern tip of the island. Explore the lighthouse trail through jungle, spot monitor lizards and hornbills, and enjoy dramatic coastal views. Entrance fee: 200 THB.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Krabi Province by ferry. Spend the afternoon at Ao Nang Beach — Krabi's most popular resort beach. Swim, sunbathe, or simply people-watch from a beach chair (50–100 THB rental). Browse the beachside shops for souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Ao Nang Walking Street comes alive at night. Explore the strip of restaurants, bars, and street food vendors. Enjoy a traditional Thai massage (300–400 THB/hour) to recover from days of island hopping.

meals.breakfast: Ao Nang or Koh Lanta café — full Western or Thai breakfast for 150–250 THB
meals.lunch: Quick bite at Ao Nang beachside food stall — pad kra pao (basil stir-fry) with a fried egg and rice for 80–120 THB
meals.dinner: Ao Nang Walking Street — try Last Fisherman Bar or a local seafood restaurant. Budget 300–450 THB per person

day_by_day.notes: Ao Nang is busier and more commercialized than Krabi Town but offers great convenience. Keep valuables secured at the beach. The national park entrance at Koh Lanta is worth the early start — go before 9 AM for the best wildlife sightings.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longtail boat from Ao Nang Beach to the famous Railay Beach — only accessible by boat (15–20 minutes, 100 THB each way). Arrive early to claim a spot on Railay West Beach before the day-trippers arrive. Swim in crystal-clear water framed by towering limestone cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the jungle trail from Railay East to Phra Nang Cave Beach — one of Thailand's most spectacular beaches. Explore the sacred Princess Cave shrine adorned with colorful offerings. Snorkel the shallow reef and explore the hidden lagoon (Diamond Cave) via a short but steep trail.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from Railay West Beach, then take the last longtail back to Ao Nang. Dinner at a local restaurant in Ao Nang or Krabi Town.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a smoothie bowl at an Ao Nang café for 150–200 THB
meals.lunch: Beach restaurant at Railay — fresh seafood, fried rice, and cold drinks. Budget 250–400 THB per person (slightly pricier due to remote location)
meals.dinner: Back in Ao Nang or Krabi Town — try khao pad sapparot (pineapple fried rice) at a local restaurant for 120–180 THB

day_by_day.notes: Railay Beach is one of the highlights of any Krabi trip — don't miss it. Wear water shoes for the rocky Railay East area. The Diamond Cave lagoon hike involves rope climbing over limestone — skip if uncomfortable with heights. Bring cash as there are no ATMs on Railay.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day — sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at your boutique hotel. Take advantage of any hotel amenities (pool, spa, garden). This is a good day to do laundry, recharge devices, and plan the second half of the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Krabi's local fresh market (Talat Kao) for a cultural deep-dive. Sample tropical fruits, observe locals going about their day, and pick up snacks. Then visit the Krabi Elephant Sanctuary or a reputable ethical animal experience in the area (book in advance, approximately 1,500–2,500 THB).
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class evening session — learn to make 3–4 classic Thai dishes including tom kha gai, pad thai, and mango sticky rice. Many local schools offer evening classes for 800–1,200 THB including market visit and recipe cards.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast — enjoy the spread at a relaxed pace
meals.lunch: Street food lunch at Talat Kao market — grilled pork skewers, sticky rice, and fresh fruit for under 150 THB
meals.dinner: Eat what you cook in your cooking class — a memorable and delicious mid-trip dinner!

day_by_day.notes: A rest day mid-trip prevents burnout and allows you to appreciate the experiences more. If the elephant sanctuary is fully booked, consider a visit to a local rubber plantation or a Thai fruit farm tour instead. Always choose ethical animal experiences that prioritize elephant welfare.

day_by_day.morning: Catch an early ferry from Krabi to Koh Phi Phi Don (approximately 1.5 hours, 350–450 THB). Check in to a guesthouse or leave bags at storage. Walk the narrow paths of Tonsai Village and climb to the famous Phi Phi Viewpoint for breathtaking panoramic views of the twin bays — one of Thailand's most iconic vistas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a snorkeling longtail boat trip around Phi Phi's stunning bays. Visit Monkey Beach, the Blue Lagoon, and snorkel at the colorful reefs around Koh Phi Phi Leh. Spot blacktip reef sharks in the shallows at Shark Point.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Phi Phi's famous beach party atmosphere at Tonsai Beach. Fire shows, beach bars, and live music create an electric atmosphere. Enjoy a sundowner at a cliff bar overlooking the bay.

meals.breakfast: Eat before the ferry or grab something at Krabi pier
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at a Tonsai Village restaurant — grilled fish and papaya salad for 200–350 THB
meals.dinner: Beachfront restaurant on Phi Phi — try the seafood BBQ buffet for 400–600 THB per person including drinks

day_by_day.notes: Koh Phi Phi is more expensive than Krabi mainland — budget accordingly. Accommodation on the island runs 800–2,000 THB/night for mid-range options. Book in advance as it fills up quickly. Keep valuables locked in your room as petty theft can occur in busy tourist areas.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up before dawn for a sunrise longtail boat tour to Maya Bay on Koh Phi Phi Leh — made famous by the movie 'The Beach.' The bay is now strictly regulated with timed entry (book in advance). Arrive early to experience it before the crowds. Entrance fee applies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Phi Phi Don and spend the afternoon at Loh Dalum Bay — the calmer, more sheltered bay on the north side of the island. Kayak the turquoise waters (200–300 THB/hour rental), explore sea caves, and relax on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the sunset ferry back to Krabi or spend a second night on Phi Phi. If returning, enjoy a quiet dinner back at your Krabi boutique hotel neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Early energy snack before the sunrise trip — grab a banana and coffee from a Tonsai bakery
meals.lunch: Beachside café on Loh Dalum Bay — club sandwich or Thai fried rice for 180–280 THB
meals.dinner: Back in Krabi — celebrate the Phi Phi adventure with a nice dinner at a riverside restaurant. Budget 350–500 THB per person

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has strict visitor limits and timed entry — book your longtail and entry permit at least 2–3 days in advance. Swimming at Maya Bay may be restricted to protect coral recovery. The sunrise visit (around 6:00–7:00 AM) is magical and worth the early start.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Hong Island (Koh Hong) — one of Krabi's best-kept secrets. Take a speedboat tour (approximately 1,000–1,500 THB) to this uninhabited island with a stunning enclosed lagoon. Kayak inside the lagoon surrounded by towering limestone walls — a surreal experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Hong Island tour with snorkeling at the surrounding reefs. Visit Lading Island and Pak Bia Island nearby for more pristine beaches and crystal-clear water. Enjoy the relative tranquility compared to busier spots like Phi Phi.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi in the late afternoon. Spend the evening at the Krabi Town Night Market (Friday–Sunday) or the Chao Fah Pier area. Browse local handicrafts, try southern Thai sweets, and relax after a day on the water.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local coffee shop — Thai-style breakfast with khao tom and side dishes for 100–150 THB
meals.lunch: Included in the Hong Island speedboat tour — beach picnic with rice boxes and fruit
meals.dinner: Krabi Town night market or a local restaurant — try kanom jeen (fermented rice noodles with curry) for 60–100 THB

day_by_day.notes: Hong Island tours are best booked through your hotel for reliability. The lagoon kayaking is the highlight — make sure your tour includes it. Bring a waterproof camera or rent an underwater housing for your phone. October may bring some swell — check conditions before booking speedboat tours.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Krabi hinterland with a half-day ATV or jungle trekking tour. Visit the Khao Phanom Bencha National Park for a nature walk through primary rainforest. Spot exotic birds, butterflies, and if lucky, gibbons. The park's waterfall trail leads to a beautiful multi-tiered cascade — entrance fee 200 THB.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the hot springs at Klong Thom (approximately 45 minutes from Krabi Town). Soak in the natural warm pools surrounded by jungle — a therapeutic experience. Nearby, the Emerald Pool (Sa Morakot) offers a stunning natural swimming pool with vivid turquoise water. Combined entry approximately 200 THB.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi for a relaxing final full evening. Treat yourself to a traditional Thai massage and a nice dinner at one of Krabi Town's better restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fuel up for the active day ahead
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near Klong Thom — simple Thai lunch with rice, vegetables, and soup for 120–200 THB
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner — try Krua Thara Restaurant by the river for fresh seafood with a view. Budget 400–600 THB per person

day_by_day.notes: The hot springs and Emerald Pool are best visited on weekdays to avoid weekend crowds. Wear swimwear under your clothes for convenience. The Emerald Pool can be crowded by midday — arrive before 10 AM or after 3 PM for a more peaceful experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final island adventure: take a longtail boat to the stunning Tonsai Beach (different from Phi Phi's Tonsai) — a hidden gem accessible only by boat or a rocky coastal walk from Railay. This laid-back beach is popular with rock climbers and has a bohemian, off-the-beaten-path vibe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Try rock climbing on the limestone cliffs above Railay or Tonsai Beach — instructors and equipment rental available for beginners (600–1,200 THB for a half-day session). Even if you don't climb, watching experienced climbers scale the vertical karst walls is spectacular. Spend remaining time swimming and relaxing.
day_by_day.evening: Last night in Krabi — make it special. Head to a rooftop bar in Ao Nang for cocktails and panoramic views. Then enjoy a farewell dinner with all your favorite Thai dishes discovered during the trip.

meals.breakfast: Slow morning at a Krabi Town café — eggs Benedict or a Thai breakfast spread for 150–250 THB
meals.lunch: Beach shack at Tonsai — simple fried rice or noodles with a cold coconut for 120–180 THB
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a favorite restaurant from the trip — splurge slightly with a seafood feast. Budget 500–700 THB per person

day_by_day.notes: Tonsai Beach is more rustic and less developed than Railay — bring cash and expect basic facilities. Rock climbing at Railay is world-class; even a beginner session is a memorable experience. Book the climbing instructor through your hotel or directly at the beach.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Krabi — wake up early for one last sunrise walk along the Krabi River promenade. Visit Wat Kaew Korawaram (the White Temple) in Krabi Town for a peaceful moment of reflection. Pick up last-minute souvenirs at the morning market — dried seafood, local spices, and Thai snacks make great gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of your boutique hotel (store luggage if needed). Enjoy a final Thai lunch in Krabi Town. Arrange transfer to Krabi International Airport for your departure flight. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Krabi. Reflect on 13 incredible days of island hopping, street food adventures, and unforgettable Thai experiences.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — savor it!
meals.lunch: Last Thai meal in Krabi Town — go back to your favorite spot from the trip or try something new. Budget 150–250 THB
meals.dinner: Airport meal or on the flight

day_by_day.notes: Pack reef-safe sunscreen, sarongs, and any liquid souvenirs in checked baggage. Keep important documents, electronics, and valuables in carry-on. The Krabi airport is small but gets busy — arrive early. Consider booking a private transfer for reliability on your departure day (400–600 THB from Krabi Town).

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Thailand Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Private airport transfer to your Krabi Province Boutique Stay. Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome drink by the pool. Take a leisurely stroll around the resort grounds to orient yourself with the stunning karst limestone scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the hotel's rooftop or poolside bar overlooking the Andaman Sea. Ease into the trip with a relaxed first evening.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: Light snack or airport lounge dining upon arrival
meals.dinner: In-hotel fine dining restaurant — try the signature Southern Thai seafood platter with fresh catch of the day, accompanied by a curated wine selection

day_by_day.notes: October is the tail end of the monsoon season in Krabi. Expect occasional showers but also lush green landscapes and fewer crowds. Pack a light rain jacket. Confirm boutique stay amenities and arrange the next day's activities with the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private long-tail boat tour of the iconic Railay Beach and Phra Nang Cave Beach — accessible only by boat. Swim in crystal-clear waters and explore the dramatic limestone cliffs. Snorkeling gear included.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rock climbing introductory session on Railay's world-famous limestone walls with a certified private guide (suitable for all levels). Alternatively, kayak through sea caves and hidden lagoons around Railay peninsula.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi Town by private speedboat. Explore the vibrant Krabi Night Market (Maharaj Road Walking Street) for an authentic street food experience.

meals.breakfast: Lavish hotel breakfast buffet featuring tropical fruits, eggs cooked to order, freshly baked pastries, and Thai congee
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood BBQ lunch at a beachside restaurant on Railay Beach — grilled tiger prawns, whole fish, and coconut rice
meals.dinner: Street food crawl at Krabi Night Market — pad thai, mango sticky rice, grilled satay skewers, and fresh coconut ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Railay Beach is only accessible by boat (15–20 min from Ao Nang). Arrange private boat transfer through the hotel concierge. Bring waterproof bags for electronics.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided trek through the Krabi Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Seua) — climb 1,237 steps to the summit for panoramic views over Krabi's mangroves, rice paddies, and karst towers. Early start recommended to beat the heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Four Islands by private speedboat — explore Koh Mor, Koh Tub, Koh Chicken, and Koh Waen. Snorkel over coral reefs and relax on pristine sandbanks that appear and disappear with the tide.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cruise back toward Krabi. Dinner at Sala Krabi or a top waterfront restaurant with views of the illuminated limestone cliffs.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — smoothie bowls, Thai omelette, and fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Picnic-style seafood lunch arranged by private boat crew on a secluded sandbank — fresh fruit, sandwiches, and cold beverages
meals.dinner: Upscale waterfront dining — whole steamed barramundi with lime and chili, massaman curry, and jasmine rice paired with a crisp Sauvignon Blanc

day_by_day.notes: Tiger Cave Temple requires modest dress (shoulders and knees covered). The sandbanks of the Four Islands are tide-dependent — confirm timing with your boat captain. Bring reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to Ao Nang pier for a premium speedboat to Koh Phi Phi Don (approx. 45 min). Check in or store luggage. Explore the vibrant village, colorful longtail boats, and the famous viewpoint hike for breathtaking panoramas of the twin bays.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private snorkeling tour around Phi Phi's best reef sites including Hin Klang and Shark Point — spot blacktip reef sharks, sea turtles, and vibrant coral gardens. Visit the iconic Maya Bay (from 'The Beach') — now carefully managed for eco-tourism.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the legendary Phi Phi sunset from the viewpoint or a clifftop bar. Enjoy the lively but upscale beach bar scene at Phi Phi Don.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a premium restaurant on Phi Phi Don — lobster thermidor or grilled whole snapper
meals.dinner: Beachside fine dining at Phi Phi — Thai tasting menu with green papaya salad, tom kha gai, and pandan-infused desserts

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has restricted visitor numbers and specific entry times — book in advance through a licensed operator. Phi Phi is a day-trip or overnight option; if overnighting, arrange boutique accommodation on Phi Phi Don through your hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning private longtail boat to Bamboo Island (Koh Mai Pai) — one of the most pristine and uncrowded islands near Phi Phi. Swim, snorkel, and relax on powdery white sand before the day-trippers arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Phi Phi Don. Indulge in a 90-minute traditional Thai massage or spa treatment at one of the island's premium wellness centers. Optional: PADI open water dive certification or fun dive with a certified dive center.
day_by_day.evening: Return by private speedboat to Krabi. Relax at the hotel pool with a cocktail before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast on Phi Phi before the boat departure — fresh fruit, yogurt, and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet picnic on Bamboo Island — artisan sandwiches, tropical fruit, sparkling water, and cold brew coffee
meals.dinner: Back in Krabi — dinner at a renowned local restaurant such as Ruen Mai, famous for authentic Southern Thai cuisine: gaeng som (sour curry), stir-fried morning glory, and crab curry

day_by_day.notes: Bamboo Island is best visited early morning. Bring plenty of drinking water and reef-safe sunscreen. Diving conditions in October can be excellent with warm water temperatures around 28–30°C.

day_by_day.morning: Private cooking class at a premium culinary school in Krabi — visit a local fresh market with your chef instructor to select ingredients, then learn to prepare 4–5 classic Thai dishes including pad kra pao, tom yum, and mango sticky rice.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at the hotel. Enjoy the pool, spa, or beachfront. Optional: private yoga session arranged through the hotel wellness program.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat cruise along the Krabi River through the mangrove forests. Spot fireflies as dusk falls — a magical experience unique to this region.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you prepared in your cooking class — a truly immersive culinary experience
meals.dinner: Intimate private dining experience arranged by the hotel — a specially curated Thai-fusion tasting menu served in a garden or on a private terrace

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class and firefly cruise in advance through the hotel concierge. The firefly boat tour is best done in October–November when firefly activity peaks. This is a perfect rest-and-recharge day.

day_by_day.morning: Premium speedboat transfer to Koh Lanta (approx. 1.5 hours). Check in to a luxury beachfront property or use as a day trip. Explore the charming Old Town (Ban Ko Lanta) — a historic fishing village with Sino-Portuguese shophouses, art galleries, and craft shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mu Ko Lanta Marine National Park and Koh Lanta's southern beaches — Had Nui and Had Khlong Chak are among the most beautiful and secluded. Snorkel in the protected marine park waters.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at a beachfront bar on Long Beach. Watch the sun dip below the Andaman horizon in a blaze of orange and pink.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at a rustic but high-quality restaurant in Koh Lanta Old Town — fresh oysters, grilled squid, and coconut soup
meals.dinner: Beachfront dinner at one of Koh Lanta's premium restaurants — slow-cooked lamb massaman, prawn green curry, and sticky rice with fresh mango

day_by_day.notes: Koh Lanta is more laid-back and less crowded than Phi Phi — ideal for those seeking a quieter island atmosphere. If overnighting, arrange boutique accommodation in advance. The Old Town is a UNESCO-recognized heritage site.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Krabi (if day-tripped to Koh Lanta) or continue exploring Koh Lanta. Visit the Thung Yee Pheng Mangrove Forest — kayak through the serene mangrove channels with a knowledgeable local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back at the Krabi boutique stay. Afternoon spa session — book a 2-hour traditional Thai herbal compress massage or aromatherapy treatment at the hotel spa.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Ao Nang's beachfront promenade. Browse boutique shops and art galleries. Enjoy a relaxed evening by the sea.

meals.breakfast: Koh Lanta hotel breakfast or café breakfast with fresh tropical juices
meals.lunch: Casual beachside lunch — fish tacos, fresh spring rolls, and coconut water
meals.dinner: Ao Nang fine dining — premium restaurant with Andaman seafood platter, crab fried rice, and Thai iced tea

day_by_day.notes: The mangrove kayak is a unique and peaceful experience — best done in the morning before the heat peaks. October rains can make mangrove ecosystems particularly lush and beautiful.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day private speedboat island-hopping adventure to the Trang Islands — Koh Ngai, Koh Kradan, and Koh Muk. These less-visited islands offer some of Thailand's most pristine beaches and untouched reefs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim through the famous Emerald Cave (Tham Morakot) on Koh Muk — a sea cave that opens into a hidden inland beach surrounded by towering cliffs, accessible only by swimming through a dark passage at low tide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi by private speedboat. Celebratory dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch on Koh Kradan — one of Thailand's most beautiful beaches — with chilled champagne, fresh seafood, and tropical fruits
meals.dinner: Hotel signature restaurant — chef's tasting menu featuring local Andaman ingredients with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The Emerald Cave can only be entered at certain tide conditions — coordinate timing with your boat captain. Bring an underwater flashlight for the cave swim. This is one of the most unforgettable experiences in Southern Thailand.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Krabi's interior — visit the Thanboke Koranee National Park botanical gardens and the stunning Bor Thor cave temples. Explore the emerald-green river and its dramatic karst surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relaxed afternoon at the hotel. Optional: private paddleboard or kayak rental along the coastline. Visit a local artisan market or browse Krabi's boutique shops for handmade souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Premium street food tour of Krabi Town with a private food guide — explore hidden local stalls, sample 10+ dishes, and learn the stories behind Southern Thai cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the national park — prepared by the hotel kitchen with local ingredients
meals.dinner: Street food tour dinner — a progressive feast through Krabi Town including boat noodles, rotee (Thai crepes), grilled corn, fresh oysters, and coconut ice cream

day_by_day.notes: The Thanboke Koranee National Park is a hidden gem — lush, peaceful, and rarely visited by tourists. The evening street food tour is a highlight for food lovers and pairs perfectly with the trip's culinary theme.

day_by_day.morning: Private boat excursion to the Hong Islands (Koh Hong) — a stunning archipelago with a hidden lagoon accessible only by kayak through a narrow sea cave. Paddle into the serene turquoise lagoon surrounded by towering limestone walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling at the vibrant coral reefs around the Hong Islands. Relax on the pristine white sand beach of Koh Hong — one of Krabi's most beautiful and protected beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset sail back to Krabi on a private traditional wooden boat. Enjoy chilled drinks and canapés on deck as the sky turns golden.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood BBQ on the boat — grilled prawns, fish, squid, with sticky rice and papaya salad
meals.dinner: Elegant dinner at a clifftop or waterfront restaurant in Ao Nang — pan-seared sea bass, red curry, and Thai dessert selection

day_by_day.notes: Koh Hong is protected by the Thai government — visitor numbers are limited. Book the private boat well in advance. The hidden lagoon is best visited at mid-tide. Bring waterproof camera gear.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga and meditation session on the beach or hotel terrace, led by a private instructor. Follow with a luxurious spa morning — full-body scrub, herbal steam, and a 60-minute hot stone massage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final island exploration — take a longtail boat to the quiet beaches of Ao Nang's nearby islands (Koh Poda or Chicken Island) for one last afternoon of swimming, sunbathing, and snorkeling in the Andaman Sea.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the hotel's finest dining venue — a curated multi-course Thai tasting menu with premium wine pairing, celebrating the end of an extraordinary journey.

meals.breakfast: Healthy spa breakfast — acai bowls, green smoothies, and granola
meals.lunch: Light beachside lunch on the island — fresh coconut, grilled fish skewers, and tropical fruit
meals.dinner: Farewell gala dinner — 6-course Thai tasting menu: amuse-bouche, tom yum consommé, lobster satay, massaman duck, mango sorbet, and coconut panna cotta with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Request a special farewell setup from the hotel — many boutique properties offer candlelit beach dinners or private terrace arrangements. This is the ideal night to splurge on an extraordinary dining experience. Begin packing and confirm departure logistics.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning at the hotel — enjoy a last swim in the pool or a walk along the beach. Savour a relaxed breakfast and soak in the last views of Krabi's magnificent karst landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out and private transfer to the airport or onward destination. Browse the airport's duty-free for Thai souvenirs — premium Thai silk, artisan coffee, and local spice blends make excellent gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Krabi. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of beaches, island hopping, and culinary discovery across one of the world's most beautiful destinations.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — a leisurely spread of your favorite dishes from the past two weeks
meals.lunch: Airport lounge dining or a final bowl of authentic khao tom (Thai rice soup) at a quality airport restaurant
meals.dinner: In-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport check-in. Krabi International Airport is small but can get busy — arrive early. Ensure all souvenirs, liquids, and duty-free items comply with airline regulations. Keep travel insurance documents and hotel receipts handy.
